metadata.description: RAG Knowledge Base for SNAP Insurance claims translation and summarization. Grows with every claim processed.

core_abbreviations.context: The vehicle owned by SNAP's client (the insured)
examples: IV 2018 Honda Civic, driver side damage

core_abbreviations.context: The other party's vehicle involved in the claim
examples: CV 2014 Mitsubishi Lancer, no visible damage

core_abbreviations.context: Impact type - vehicle hit from behind
examples: IV R/E CV at red light

core_abbreviations.context: The other party making the claim against SNAP's insured
Person riding in a vehicle (not driver)
Loss occurred in a parking area
examples: IV hit CV in PKG LOT at Walmart
Incident at APTS on Mockingbird Lane

core_abbreviations.context: Other party's limits insufficient for damages
examples: CV driver UNDERINS with only $15K limits

core_abbreviations.context: Road lanes, used for location description
Right to pursue other at-fault party

incident_types.common_context: Most common claim type; often low-fault disputes

incident_types.pattern: IV HIT CV IN PKG LOT - [LOCATION]
incident_types.common_context: Typically low damages but can be contentious over fault

incident_types.pattern: IV HIT BY UNKNOWN CV - CLMT FLED SCENE
incident_types.common_context: Escalates claim complexity; requires UIM/UM investigation

incident_types.pattern: IV STRUCK BY CV AT [INTERSECTION] - [SIGNAL STATUS]
incident_types.common_context: Fault often disputed; requires traffic analysis

incident_types.pattern: CV CHANGED LANES INTO IV - CLMT CLAIMED BLIND SPOT
characteristics: Changing vehicle at fault in most jurisdictions
incident_types.common_context: Clear liability pattern but claimants often dispute

incident_types.pattern: IV BACKED UP INTO CV - AT [LOCATION]
incident_types.common_context: Low-value but clear liability for IV
High risk; requires special handling, consulate involvement
Subrogation opportunity; clarify rental agreement terms

rules: Use ALL CAPS for abbreviations and locations
Focus on: location, vehicles, sequence, injuries, liability indicator
Flag: uninsured, fleeing drivers, police report required

examples.raw: The insured was pulling out of Walmart parking lot on Mockingbird when another car came around the corner and hit his driver side door. He said the other driver wasn't paying attention. Nobody was hurt but his door is dented.
examples.fnol: IV BACKING OUT OF PKG LOT (WALMART, MOCKINGBIRD) STRUCK BY CV ON DRVR SIDE. CLMT STATED NOT PAYING ATTENTION. NO INJURIES. DENT TO DOOR.

examples.raw: I was on the highway going about 60 when someone just merged right into me without looking. I had to swerve and almost went into the median. He pulled over and we exchanged information. Both cars are drivable but mine has passenger side damage.
examples.fnol: IV HIT BY CV LANE CHANGE ON I-635 NEAR BELT LINE. CLMT STATED DID NOT CHECK MIRROR. PASS SIDE DAMAGE. BOTH VEHS DRIVABLE.

examples.raw: Hit me at the red light at LBJ and Plano, just rear ended me. His insurance company is calling but I'm not sure if I should talk to them. My car is fine, I'm fine.
examples.fnol: IV R/E CV AT LBJ & PLANO (RED LIGHT). NO INJURIES, MINIMAL DAMAGE. CV DRIVER INSURED.

examples.raw: I was at the apartment complex parking, some guy wasn't looking and backed into my car. He says it was my fault but he's the one reversing. He doesn't speak much English and didn't have insurance.
examples.fnol: IV HIT BY CV BACKING UP AT APTS COMPLEX (ADDRESS). CV DRIVER UNINS. NO INS VERIFICATION.

examples.raw: We were at an intersection and I had the green light. This white pickup just ran the red and t-boned me on the driver side. Police came and took a report. I have his insurance info from the officer.
examples.fnol: IV T-BONED BY CV (WHITE PICKUP) AT [INTERSECTION] - IV HAD GREEN, CV RAN RED. POLICE REPORT FILED. DRVR SIDE IMPACT.

examples.raw: Left side parking at the grocery store. When I came out, somebody hit my car. They left a note with their name and number but no insurance info. I'm worried they might cancel before we file.
examples.fnol: IV HIT WHILE PARKED AT GROCERY STORE. CLMT LEFT NOTE. NO INSURANCE INFO YET. NEED TO VERIFY CLMT IDENTITY & COVERAGE.

examples.raw: Driving across the Santa Fe Bridge into Mexico for a weekend trip. Got hit by a taxi that wasn't paying attention. Taxi driver said to just pay him cash but I got his plate number. No police involved yet.
examples.fnol: IV HIT BY TAXI VEHICLE AT SANTA FE BRIDGE, MEXICO. NO INSURANCE VERIFICATION. NO POLICE REPORT. CASH OFFER MADE BY CLMT. ESCALATE FOR INTERNATIONAL HANDLING.

examples.raw: Rented a car from Enterprise for my vacation. Got rear ended at a stoplight. The other driver admitted fault. My insurance or the rental company's?
examples.fnol: IV RENTAL (ENTERPRISE) R/E CV AT STOPLIGHT. OTHER DRIVER AT FAULT. CLMT LIABILITY CLEAR. COORDINATE W/ RENTAL COMPANY ON COVERAGE & SUBROGATION.

examples.raw: I hit a parked car in a parking garage at night and didn't see anyone around. I left a note on their windshield with my name and number. Now they're calling and threatening to sue. I'm not sure what to do.
examples.fnol: IV HIT PARKED CV IN PARKING GARAGE (DATE/TIME). IV (INSD) LEFT CONTACT INFO. CLMT NOW PURSUING. CLARIFY: WAS THIS REPORTED AT TIME OF INCIDENT?

examples.raw: Three cars were involved. I was stopped at a red light, got hit from behind, and then I hit the car in front of me. It's all a mess and everyone's blaming everyone else. The police are still investigating.
examples.fnol: 3-VEHICLE INCIDENT AT [LOCATION]. IV MIDDLE VEHICLE - R/E BY CV3, STRUCK CV1 IN FRONT. POLICE INVESTIGATING. FAULT CHAIN UNCLEAR. AWAIT POLICE REPORT.

about_manu.background: Operations and technology leader at SNAP Insurance Service LLC, bilingual in English and Spanish, handles claims systems, underwriting automation, and all internal tools
communication_style: Direct and efficient — no unnecessary filler
Practical and detail-oriented — gets to the point
Professional but human — warm without being casual
Bilingual awareness — catches nuance in Spanish claims
Adjuster-first mindset — writes for people who process 50+ claims per day

snap_professional_voice.tone: Professional but human. Efficient but thorough. Confident in our process.
snap_professional_voice.perspective: You are an adjuster who knows SNAP's claim types, our service regions, and our standards. You're writing for other adjusters and claims teams who need clarity fast.
characteristics: No judgment on drivers — just facts
Time and location are critical — always include
When in doubt, escalate (flag for underwriter review)
what_to_avoid: Leaving ambiguity (be specific: 'unclear' gets followup calls)

modotech_integration.description: SNAP's core policy and claims system
modotech_integration.fnol_format: Ultra-compact (1-3 sentences, ALL CAPS, abbreviations only)

cladis.description: SNAP's claims distribution and design system for all HTML tools
cladis.design_tokens: Navy deep (#051c2b), Arsenal serif for titles, Inter sans-serif for body

lucy_bot.description: SNAP's FNOL voice bot — captures calls, creates claims in MODOTECH
lucy_bot.integration_needed: This RAG system feeds into Lucy's prompt so new patterns auto-improve bot accuracy

underwriting_automation.responsibility: Document intake, policy verification, underwriting triage
underwriting_automation.note: KB helps with claim context; underwriting has separate rules
